coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 'specific and good coverage of 14A neurons in both the larval and adult VNCs, except one motor neuron in adult T1 segments'
quote: In decapitated animals, activation drove the femur-tibia joint to move anteriorly, most pronounced in the middle legs. We also observed flexion of the legs.
other_observation: Video 42 montage shows a decapitated fly on a platform with 'ON' marked frames during stimulation.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 'specific and provides good coverage of 17A neurons in the adult and larval VNCs. A small SEZ cluster, likely 17A neurons, and a medial brain cluster are also marked.'
quote: Activation of 17 A neurons drove flexion of all the leg segments in both decapitated and intact animals.
other_observation: In the video-48 montage the fly is crouched with the legs drawn under the body through the ON frames and stands again after the stimulus.
notes: 'flexion of all the leg segments' taken to cover the legs generally (d2-d4 yes); the lateral view in video 48 shows front, middle and hind legs flexed during the ON frames. A stricter reading of 'leg segments' would make d2-d4 unclear.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 'Very specific and good coverage of 21A neurons in both adult and larval VNC. A motor neuron in T1, likely from another lineage is marked as well.'

notes: 'flexion of the legs' counts for d2-d4; body lowered and held gives d5 yes. Table 2 attributes videos 52/53 to the tj line, while Supplementary file 5 gives the ey line genotype for those videos (see notes.md).

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 'Very specific and good coverage of 21A neurons in both adult and larval VNC. A motor neuron in T1, likely from another lineage is marked as well.'

notes: Coded from the 'similar phenotype' statement; same cells as the decapitated record.

coverage_notes: Supplementary file 1: 'specific and provides good coverage of 23B neurons in the larval and adult VNCs. Some chordatonal sensory neurons are marked as well.'
quote: Activation caused intact animals to fall on their back due to uncoordinated leg movements and sustained flexion or extension of the leg segments
other_observation: Same Table 2 cell: 'Flies also showed increased grooming activity. We also observed wing buzzing in response to activation.' These support d9, d11 and d13.
notes: 'leg movements'/'leg segments' without naming which legs: d2-d4 unclear. 'sustained flexion or extension' gives d5 and d6 yes; 'uncoordinated leg movements' gives d7 yes; grooming d9 yes; wing buzzing d11 and d13 yes.
